args.text: [lane-ibis] Three risks of caching DNS (Domain Name System, the internet's address book) answers for too long: (1) Stale addresses: users are sent to a server that has moved or been retired, so services fail or time out. (2) Slow recovery: when a site switches to a backup server during an outage, cached answers keep traffic pointed at the broken one. (3) Lingering bad answers: if a poisoned or wrongly changed record is cached, it keeps misleading users long after the fix.

[lane-ibis] Idempotent (safe to repeat) retries matter because networks fail in ways that leave the sender unsure whether a request worked, so it must be able to try again. If repeating a request has the same effect as sending it once, a retry cannot cause double charges, duplicate orders or other repeated side effects.
